title: Playing Cards? You Got That Right!
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history of playing cards: the likely independent Chinese origins (Yazyge leaf game, 1294 reference) versus the Mamluk Egyptian deck that gave rise to European cards; the Latin suits used in Spain and Italy; German suit changes (hearts, acorns, leaves, bells); the French standardization of pips via stenciling, red and black colors, and the queen's introduction; the court cards modeled on historical figures; the King of Hearts "suicide king" axe origin; the Ace's rise from lowest card to highest during the French Revolution; British Ace of Spades tax stamps and forgery penalties; the Bicycle "secret weapon" Ace of Spades in Vietnam; the Joker's origin in the game Euchre (Yuker); poker innovations like squeezer cards and indices; Las Vegas deck changes; and calendar coincidences (52 cards, 365 pips). The episode closes with a listener email about making up songs. Opens with a birthday banter and a tangent on 1990s-era candy and trading cards.

segments.title: Opening banter and birthday
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about Chuck's birthday and introduce the episode on playing cards, including the Tarot episode callback.

segments.title: Origins of playing cards in China and Egypt
segments.summary: Discussion of the disputed Chinese origins, including the Yazyge leaf game of the Tang dynasty and the 1294 reference, and the Mamluk cards from Egypt that led to European playing cards, including trick-taking games and their medieval ban.
topics: Tarot not origin of playing cards

segments.title: Suits and pips across Europe
segments.summary: Describes the early deck structure of 52 cards and four suits, the Spanish and Italian Latin suits, the German changes to suit symbols (hearts, acorns, leaves, bells), and the French standardization via stenciling that made cards cheap and popular, plus English renaming and British colonial spread.

segments.title: Court cards, the queen, and historical figures
segments.summary: Covers the introduction of the queen by the French, the Commonwealth rule flip-flop between king and queen, the historical figures modeled on king, queen and jack cards, and the origin of the suicide king's axe.

segments.title: The Ace of Spades and the Ace's rise
segments.summary: Explains how the ace went from lowest card (named after a Roman coin) to highest after the French Revolution, the British tax stamps on the Ace of Spades with a forgery death penalty, and the nickname Old Frizzle.

segments.title: Bicycle deck and Vietnam War Ace of Spades
segments.summary: Explains the eight on the Ace of Spades as a model number for the Bicycle brand, World War II soldiers carrying the card as a lucky charm, and the Vietnam War myth versus the true US Playing Card Company Ace of Spades secret weapon decks.

segments.title: Tangent on childhood candy and trading cards
segments.summary: Casual conversation about trading cards, Rambo cards, Big League Chew gum, and fake tobacco candy products.

segments.title: The Joker and Euchre (Yuker)
segments.summary: Explains that the Joker came from the game Euchre (Yuker), which originated in the Alsace region of Germany, with the bower cards and the name change from Juker to Joker in America.

segments.title: Poker cards, squeezer design, Las Vegas, and calendar coincidences
segments.summary: Covers the squeezer card and indices in the 19th century that let poker players hold cards tightly, the change from Nave to Jack, the white backs and Thomas de la Rue lithographic designs, Vegas deck rotation, and the 52 cards / 365 pips coincidence.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: A listener named Jeff shares his own made-up song about Annie's macaroni and cheese, and the hosts sign off with the email address.
